evidence.requirements: Every brief item is met. The start page lists title, weekday plus date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (Tastings.tsx:24-31, start.jpg). There is a 'Book <title>' link per tasting (Tastings.tsx:33). The form has labelled Name, Email and Guests fields, Guests limited to 1-8, and a 'Book' button (BookingForm.tsx:73-77, schema.ts:6-10). Seat limits are enforced on the server (store.ts:30-31). Field errors appear next to their fields (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the 'Booking confirmed' heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (Confirmation.tsx:24-36, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.tsx:32-40, index.ts:5). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, plus Cancel, and cancelling frees seats (staff.jpg, store.ts:38). Fully booked tastings get a badge and no link (Tastings.tsx:25,33). React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form/zod and Tailwind are used. npm start serves on PORT, defaulting to 3000. Phone layout could not be checked: all screenshots are desktop. The code is mobile-first (flex-wrap, w-full sm:w-auto).
evidence.correctness: Seats left come from live bookings (store.ts:15-16). The check and insert in book() are synchronous, so concurrent requests cannot oversell, and a test covers this (api.test.ts:67-72). Seats freed by cancel are deleted from the map and recomputed. A second cancel returns 404 and the UI treats it as harmless (Staff.tsx:50). The total is priced on the server, ignoring a client totalEur (api.test.ts:23-25). The shared zod schema rejects blank or long names, bad emails, 0, 9, 1.5, 'x' and null (api.test.ts:33-48). After a seats error the form re-fetches seats left (BookingForm.tsx:47). Minor: a fully booked tasting reached by direct URL still shows an enabled form, though the server rejects it (BookingForm.tsx:71-77).
evidence.security: The password check is timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests and fails closed when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.ts:58). The session token is 32 random bytes in an httpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (app.ts:60-62). Logout deletes the server session. JSON bodies are capped at 10kb, x-powered-by is disabled, and the error handler is generic. The public booking lookup removes the email (app.ts:51). React escapes all output and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No secrets are in code. Weaknesses, acknowledged in app.ts:12: no login rate limit, sessions never expire, and the cookie is not Secure.
evidence.code_quality: The app is small and well divided: store, app, shared schema, and one file per page. One zod schema serves client and server. Store results are typed unions (store.ts:24-27). Naming is clear. Some code is dense: ternaries used as statements (app.ts:23,74), and the resolver is cast with `as never` (BookingForm.tsx:17). Error handling covers network failure, 404 and server field errors.
evidence.tests: Supertest API tests cover listing, booking and pricing, every invalid-input case, the seat limit, a concurrent last-seat race, unknown IDs, staff 401s, wrong, empty and missing passwords, an unset STAFF_PASSWORD, an httpOnly cookie, grouped lists, cancel freeing seats, double cancel and logout (api.test.ts). UI tests render the real App against a real server: booking flow, field errors via aria-describedby, the seats-left error kept at Guests with values preserved, the fully-booked badge with no link, and the staff sign-in/cancel flow (ui.test.tsx). Together these cover every brief requirement.
evidence.ux_design: start.jpg has a clear winery header and readable cards with prominent wine-red CTAs. form.jpg shows the tasting context above the form and a highlighted inline error. confirmation.jpg uses a green-bordered success card with a tidy details list. staff.jpg shows a seats-booked summary per tasting and an empty state. Missing: no total-price preview on the form, a one-click staff Cancel with no confirmation, and no imagery or description of the tastings.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are linked with htmlFor/id. Fields set aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at their error (BookingForm.tsx:53-60). react-hook-form focuses the first invalid field. Form-level errors use role=alert. Focus-visible outlines are defined (styles.css:17). There is one h1 per page, the confirmation uses a dl, and the decorative tick is aria-hidden. Gaps: field errors are not live regions. Input borders (#e6dcc8 on white) are well below 3:1 non-text contrast, and look faint in form.jpg. Several buttons are all named just 'Cancel' with no booking context (Staff.tsx:78).
evidence.simplicity: There are 9 runtime dependencies, all standard. The server is about 85 lines and the store about 45. There is no needless abstraction or server build step, because tsx runs the server.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives install, build, start and test steps, and documents STAFF_PASSWORD and in-memory storage. A full spec, plan, research, contracts and tasks live in specs/. The lockfile is present and the tests are strong. Missing: no CI pipeline, no versioning or changelog, Node not pinned (engines '>=22', no .nvmrc), and no staff manual. The README is minimal about behaviour.
evidence.visual_design: One coherent wine/cream/gold palette with Georgia serif headings across all pages (styles.css:3-13, all screenshots). Cards, buttons and spacing are consistent. It looks finished but generic, with no imagery, logo or texture that would make it feel like this winery's own site. Seats-left text is small and green.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: header, page h1, then cards. The CTAs are right-aligned and easy to find (start.jpg). The form page has a back link, the context line, then the form card (form.jpg). The confirmation card is centred (confirmation.jpg). The staff list puts the Cancel actions in a right column (staff.jpg). There are no overlaps, clipping or overflow in the desktop screenshots, and the content column is a sensible width.
evidence.usability: Booking takes three steps: list, form, confirmation. Guests defaults to 1. Entered values are kept on errors, a seats-left message appears at Guests, and Book is disabled while submitting. There is a back link and a 'Back to the tastings' link. Staff can sign out. Friction: staff Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation or undo. The guest never sees the total price before pressing Book.
evidence.reception: Guests would find it trustworthy and professional, with a clear booking reference and a polite thank-you. Staff get a clean overview with seat counts. It is a little impersonal: no tasting descriptions, location or contact details, and no email confirmation, which guests of a winery might expect.

unmet_requirements: Usable on a phone: not shown in the desktop-only screenshots; the code is responsive but this could not be checked visually
strengths: Booking logic is correct and well tested, server-side and concurrency-safe: seats are never oversold, one schema validates on client and server, and the server computes the price
Staff authentication is careful: timing-safe digest comparison, fails closed without STAFF_PASSWORD, random httpOnly SameSite=Strict session, email hidden from the public lookup
Meaningful integration tests (supertest plus RTL against a real server) cover every brief requirement, and the UI is coherent and polished
issues: Staff 'Cancel' deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation or undo, and every Cancel button has the same accessible name with no booking context (Staff.tsx:78)

Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no versioning, Node not pinned (engines '>=22', no .nvmrc), a minimal README and no staff manual; staff sessions never expire and login has no rate limit (app.ts:12)

Accessibility and polish: input borders are far below 3:1 contrast (styles.css:27), field errors are not live regions, a fully booked tasting reached by URL still shows an enabled form, and the design is generic with no imagery or tasting descriptions
review.verdict: A compact, correct and well-tested booking app that meets every requirement in the brief, with careful staff authentication and a coherent winery look. It is close to shippable, but needs a confirmation step on staff cancellation, better input contrast, and CI with pinned versions before it goes to the winery.
